[b]September 17, 2026: We dont care if it is against International Law, International Law is against us![/b]

With the EDU attempting to stabilise itself in the White Strait and re-assert its position against THEP and Thýven, the government of Thýven needed to act with rapid action. 

Thus with the deployment of ships into the outer borders of the USOs international waters, Thýven would move to consolidate the Elseyr front. 

In the past Thýven had weaponised its control of the entrance to the White Strait in order to pressure the EDU into submission, these attempts prior had failed primarily due to international law and the general need for order. However, with the EDU clearly setting itself up as an aggressive opponent to THEP, the need for a rebuttal would lead to members of the Gøsfodde to reconsider Thývens stance on international law.

After a six hour long debate in the chambers, with several walk-outs occurring from members of the opposition, the Gøsfodde would pass the Defending Elseyr Act thereby permitting the armed forces of Thýven and the Patriarchate to act in full capacity, even against international law under a specialised mandate of defense.

Thus, Patriarch Mendenav, armed with the new mandate, would issue an order to blockade Thývenic sea lanes that ran through the strait to all members of the EDU, closing ports and other shipping lanes to both warships, and cargo ships. A stark warning would be sent to the EDU, stating that any EDU vessel that attempts to break the blockade would be sunk under the conventions of the wartime mandate.

The patriarchate would state politely in a press briefing summarising the shift in doctrine as We dont care if it is against International Law, International Law is against us.

[u][b]USO National Emergency Alert[/b][/u] 

September 21, 2026

People of the USO. Today Mr. Thýven tries to play dirty, but we will not let them bully the United States of Oceanic. We do not seek total war, but this is a warning with a deadline. In 144 hours, if Thýven does not withdraw its ships or come to the table with peaceful diplomacy alongside the EDU, then a nuclear strike will be our final message. Both the EDU and the USO will use force if they refuse to respect fair international law. We have the numbers of our strike forces at sea and on land, ready to deliver heavy punishment. God bless the USO."

Admiral Aviek Husk steps onto the deck of the command carrier, the boots a constant reminder of what three flattops can project into a theatre. Admiral Aviek Husk watches the deck crews finish the last of the cat shots while the staff feeds me details that USO has prepared a fleet of three aircraft carriers, twenty destroyers, thirty-four frigates, five cruisers, twenty corvettes, thirty conventional submarines, four nuclear boats, and one hundred and ninety patrol craft arrayed across the White Strait corridor. Admiral Aviek Husk runs the numbers in his head and feels the weight of it and the carriers each carry an air group drawn from USO's broader inventory, the surface fleet bristling with over twenty Aegis-type escorts and long-range strike cells, while the submarines slip undetected and ready to strike with order.

My orders are simple, Admiral Aviek Husk told the flag officers crowded in the wardroom. Hold the line, keep the lanes open, and make the cost of breaking the blockade unacceptable. They nod; the tactical display blinks with target tracks and transit lanes. We have allocated the naval missile reserves for maritime denial. Nine hundred and twenty-nine conventional long-range strike missiles are ready to be kernel-launched by surface combatants and submarines to shape an adversarys behavior without touching the nuclear threshold. The carrier wings will provide persistent air coverage for convoys and hunting packs of enemy vessels while land-based fighters lend reach from our coastal bases.

There is a different line drawn on the blueprints of escalation, and I am not the one to erase it. Four nuclear submarines form the hard core of our strategic risk but order to use in foces if Thýven take a one of close to war. They are dispersed and on patrol their mere presence rewrites calculus in the capitals watching this unfold. We will not brandish them lightly, nor will we pretend they are decorative eight hundred and one strategic warheads and a further one hundred and twenty tactical charges sit under the Sovereign Nuclear Deterrent Commands oversight, but those numbers exist to deter annihilation, not to solve a blockade. The message to the Patriarchate is surgical and unambiguous, and possess the means to punish existential aggression, but until the last conventional option has been exhausted, we will lean on precision, presence, and the massed conventional missiles in our inventory.

On the tactical net, the destroyer squadrons report their stations, twenty ships in picket, layered screens surrounding the carriers and interdicting choke points; thirty conventional submarines running covert ASW sweeps; one hundred and ninety patrol boats seurcing the merchant traffic and shepherding the first convoys through contested waters. Our amphibious and special operations units stand ready, but the goal is to move the adversary by pressure, not by war. If threated from the Gøsfodde, fiery phrases about casting off international law. Oredr will reply with the only heavt strike from sea and land relentless, visible capability. Every missile we posture, every cruiser that crosses their horizon, subtracts an option from their playbook.

At 02:12 local, the order goes out maintain escalation discipline, engage only under pre-set rules of engagement, and keep our submarines and carriers in vectored positions that make their intent unmistakable. Admiral Aviek Husk feel the stress within the command, and a cold understanding that three carriers, twenty destroyers, thirty-four frigates, five cruisers, twenty corvettes, thirty conventional submarines, four nuclear boats, and one hundred and ninety patrol craft are ready for total war if ditplcae doesn't work out. If diplomacy frays, we will first use the nine hundred and twenty-nine conventional long-range missiles to dismantle the blockade, to sever supply nodes and deny ports, reserving the nuclear option four nculear and their strategic weight only for the contingency that would end the state itself.

[b]September 22, 2025: Save the World First, Orthodoxy Second.[/b]

The ultimatum by the USO shook the government of Thýven, nuclear weapons aimed now at Thývens shores was unthinkable, and indeed shook even the most loyal Mendenavist. Yet it seemed to most that the patriarch was set upon his track.

As a result a fracture would appear in the hours following the ultimatum as loyal Mendenavists sought quickly a resolution to the matter, attempting to rapidly pass legislation to revoke the order, however, hardliners proved a major block on any revocation of the order, utilising the ideal of Patriarchal Infallibility to defend the actions of the patriarch.

In the meantime the nobility of Thýven, fed up with the shenanigans of the church would move to back an emergency coalition formed by the Doge of the Free Republic of Knygta and Deyn, Albus Capricorn, who had vowed to end the blockade within 24 hours, and dethrone the patriarch.

However the promise came with a caveat, the formation of a neutral emergency government under the governance of solely the Gøsfodde with Capricorn as the temporary head of state, something which few nobles were willing to accept, fearing that the more liberal Capricorn would attempt to use his Republic's wealth to influence the trajectory of the government.

Unable to verbally command the legislature, Capricorn thus moved to assert his power physically, ordering the Merchant Navy of the Free Republic of Knygta and Deyn to be raised to full combat mode with plans to face the blockade, hoping to break it internally.

While to some this was a laughable attempt to gain legitimacy under a heavily centralised Mendenavist government, it became clear that Capricorn was serious in his threats as the Navy of the Republic quickly made its way to the rear of the blockade, armed and ready to fire. Furthermore was the threat of Knygta and Deyn using its own rocket arsenal and SRBM arsenal against Thýven itself to restore order.

Thus, as the navy made its appearance on the blockade, the Gøsfodde would assemble under the guise of preventing a potentially destabilising civil war, led by Piter Drømm a series of declarations were made.

[list]
1. The Mendenavist government is stripped of its powers under the 1865 constitution
2. The Patriarchate will be stripped of legislative and executive powers effective immediately.
3. The armed forces of Thýven will be temporarily recalled from all international positions.
4. An emergency government will be formed under the leadership of the Gøsfodde, acting as executive and legislative.
[/list]

With the orders being issued and promulgated, the government of Thýven would signal internationally that it would be lifting the blockade for The stability and freedom of Erene, along with a two week period of full withdrawal of all armed forces from centres of conflict in the White Strait and the Baliwick Sea.
